newsitem.title: INDIA: Three killed in Kashmir attack on poll candidate.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in Kashmir attack on poll candidate.

text.p: At least three people were killed and five wounded when security guards of a political candidate on Friday opened fire when he was attacked by suspected separatist guerrillas, witnesses said.

Officials said the shootings took place in downtown Srinagar, summer capital of the state of Jammu and Kashmir, when the assailants fired on Janata Dal party candidate Ashraf Mirza, who escaped unhurt.
The dead included a police officer. More than five people were injured, police said.
At least 20 political activists have been killed and more than 12 candidates have escaped bids on their lives during the election campaign, which began in late August.
The leader of Kashmir's biggest National Conference party, Farooq Abdullah, escaped a grenade attack by separatist rebels during an election rally on Thursday.
Abdullah was addressing the rally in Muran village, 32 km (20 miles) south of Srinagar, when the grenade exploded behind the stage but injured no one.
Abdullah was state chief minister in 1990 when a separatist rebellion erupted in the Himalayan province.

The National Conference party is widely expected to win this month's elections, the first state assembly polls since 1987, and Abdullah is tipped to become chief minister. The regional party has candidates in all of the state's 87 constituencies.

On Wednesday, suspected militants threw a grenade at the home of Mufti Mohammad Syed, former federal home (interior) minister and a regional Congress party leader, in Bijbehara town, 40 km (25 miles) south of Srinagar. No one was injured.
The first day of polling in the four-stage elections took place on September 7. More voting was set for September 16, 21 and 30, and results are expected the first week of October.

Dozens of militant groups are fighting for either independence or a merger with neighbouring Pakistan. Insurgency-related violence has killed more than 20,000 since the separatist revolt began, police and hospital officials say.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training the guerrillas, while Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
